chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the visitation of the House on the Day of Sacrifice.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Visit it. If you are occupied, it will not harm you to visit the House the next day, but do not delay visiting it from your day, for it is disliked for the Mutamatti' to delay it, and it is permissible for the Mufrid to delay it.'

When you come to the House on the Day of Sacrifice and stand at the door of the Mosque, say: 'O Allah, help me in my ritual acts, save me for it, and present it to me. I ask You with the request of the humble, the lowly, the one confessing his sin, that You forgive my sins and return me with my need fulfilled.'

O Allah, I am Your servant, the land is Your land, and the House is Your House. I have come seeking Your mercy and following Your command, pleased with Your decree. I ask You with the request of the needy to You, the obedient to Your command, the fearful of Your punishment, the afraid of Your retribution.

That You grant me Your pardon and save me from the Fire by Your mercy. Then come to the Black Stone, kiss it, and touch it. If you cannot, touch it with your hand and kiss your hand. If you cannot, face it and say Allahu Akbar.

And say as you said when you circumambulated the House on the day you arrived in Mecca. Then circumambulate the House seven circuits, as I described to you on the day you arrived in Mecca. Then pray two rak'ahs near the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), reciting in them 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun'.
Then return to the Black Stone, kiss it if you can, or face it and say Allahu Akbar. Then go out to al-Safa, climb it, and do as you did on the day you entered Mecca.

Then go to al-Marwah, climb it, and circumambulate between them seven circuits, starting with al-Safa and ending with al-Marwah. When you do that, you have been released from all restrictions you entered with, except for women.

Then return to the House and circumambulate it another circuit. Then pray two rak'ahs near the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Then you have been released from everything, and you have completed your Hajj entirely, and everything you were restricted from.

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: When he does that, he has been released from everything he was restricted from, except women. Then he returns to the House, circumambulates one circuit, and prays two rak'ahs, and he has been released from everything he was restricted from. The circumambulation of women is obligatory with Hajj and Umrah for men, women, the elderly, and the eunuchs, and touching women is not permissible except after this circumambulation.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One who performs Umrah then Hajj in the same season
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rituals and supplications for visiting the Kaaba on the Day of Sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed procedural guide for the Hajj rituals on the Day of Sacrifice, distinguishing between the *Mutamatti'* and *Mufrid* regarding the timing of their Tawaf. It emphasizes the spiritual significance of the supplication at the Kaaba's door and the specific acts of kissing or touching the Black Stone, culminating in the release from Ihram restrictions after completing the Sa'i and a final Tawaf. The text also clarifies that the Tawaf of the women is a mandatory obligation for both men and women, linking the physical rites to their legal and spiritual completion.
